professional_profile.note: Source: Application_Differentiators_and_Professional_Profile.pdf. Use these to shape the narrative/voice of CVs and cover letters — they describe how Jacqueline works, not new hard skills.

differentiators.title: Validate, then optimize
points: Builds first, measures the outcome, then improves it.
Work guided by evidence rather than assumptions.
Examples: algorithm optimization, AI token optimization, software architecture refinement, data-driven LinkedIn experiments.

differentiators.title: Bridge business and technology
points: Translates business requirements into technical solutions.
Considers maintainability, scalability, stakeholder needs and business value — not just implementation.

differentiators.title: Systems thinking
points: Prefers understanding how an entire system works and how its components interact.

differentiators.title: Continuous learning
points: Deliberately explores unfamiliar technologies and underlying concepts instead of staying in one stack.
Focuses on principles that transfer across tools and frameworks.

differentiators.title: Optimization mindset
points: Enjoys improving performance, architecture, workflows, learning processes and engineering practices.
Optimization is a recurring pattern across her projects.

differentiators.title: Build before claiming expertise
points: Demonstrates competence through projects and practical work rather than broad claims about expertise.

differentiators.title: Intellectual honesty
points: Comfortable changing her opinion when new evidence appears.
Communicates uncertainty honestly while actively working toward understanding.

differentiators.title: AI as an engineering tool
points: Uses AI to support reasoning, architecture, experimentation and productivity — not as a substitute for engineering judgment.

differentiators.title: Ownership
points: Interests naturally extend toward architecture, communication, leadership, requirements engineering and long-term product thinking.

professional_profile.core_differentiator_narrative: Her strongest differentiator is not a specific programming language or framework. It is her habit of understanding complete systems, measuring outcomes, making thoughtful engineering decisions, and continuously improving solutions.
professional_profile.engineering_philosophy_quote: The projects I enjoy most are the ones where I can understand a system end-to-end, make thoughtful architectural decisions, measure the results, and iteratively improve the solution. That is the way I like to work, whether I am building backend software, designing AI workflows, or collaborating with stakeholders.
personal_positioning: Software Engineer with Architecture and AI Focus.
Engineer who enjoys understanding complex systems and making them better.
Someone who values thoughtful engineering, continuous learning and measurable improvement.
four_questions_every_application_answers: What kinds of problems do I enjoy solving?
How do I approach unfamiliar technologies?
What evidence demonstrates how I work?
Why does that make me valuable for this specific role?

github_repositories.honesty_rules: Only 'flagship_own' and 'secondary_own' are genuinely her own substantive work. 'assessment_takehomes' are job trial tasks (label as such). 'open_source_contribution' is a fork with one small commit. 'learning_selfstudy' are course-along/scaffold repos. All quantitative performance/test figures are the repos' own README claims and are not independently verified.

flagship_own.name: Automated Telegram-Signal Execution System (Signal Pipeline)
flagship_own.dates: 2026-03 to 2026-04 (~2 months, very high cadence: 192 + 168 commits)
flagship_own.description: Self-built distributed system that receives German-language execution signals from ~32 Telegram channels, parses them, and auto-executes trades on MT 5 with a multi-gate risk-management pipeline and a FastAPI web dashboard. SignalApp is the earlier iteration; SignalTelegramParser ('Signal Pipeline') is the more mature, English-documented evolution — present as ONE evolving project, not two.
learnings: Reliability engineering: dual push+poll signal delivery with dedup cache keyed on (chat_id, msg_id, text_hash)
Layered risk gates (auto SL/TP, SL tightening, spread gate, equity-based risk cap with documented float tolerance)
Integrating a legacy GUI execution platform (MT5) over RPyC, containerized under Wine+VNC
flagship_own.tests: Extensive; README claims 227 tests (parsers, risk guards, DB, API, trade service).
flagship_own.relevance: high — strongest portfolio piece: real distributed architecture, reliability/risk design, large test suite, strong docs.
flagship_own.caveat: Handles real money/credentials; keep private. Overlaps with SignalApp — cite as one project.

flagship_own.name: Algorithmic Execution & Backtesting System (execution framework)
flagship_own.description: Quant execution system on the execution framework framework running 10 walk-forward-validated mean-reversion/momentum strategies live on MT5, plus a large research/backtesting harness (scans 205 symbols x 17 signal types; README claims ~130M backtests) with composite-score ranking and Monte Carlo portfolio simulation.
learnings: Quantitative research pipeline (strategy scanning, walk-forward validation, two-stage promotion gate, Monte Carlo risk-of-ruin)
Writing a custom adapter into a third-party execution framework
Strategy design, position sizing, drawdown/risk modeling
flagship_own.tests: Present (~10 test modules; README claims 57 unit tests).
flagship_own.relevance: high — shows quantitative/algorithmic depth distinct from CRUD/integration work.
flagship_own.caveat: This maps to the existing 'Execution Research & Backtesting Platform' project entry. The sibling repo 'ExecutionSystemApp-highspeed-backtest-' is an earlier snapshot of the SAME project — do NOT count twice.

flagship_own.name: Laravel Auth & CSV Import (Sanctum API + session)
flagship_own.description: Laravel 11 app demonstrating two auth approaches (Sanctum token auth for a JSON API + session-based web login) and CSV contact import via PhpSpreadsheet.
learnings: Interface-driven service-layer architecture (AuthentificationInterface, FileHandlerInterface -> Sanctum/Session/CSV services)
Progressive refactoring (auth logic out of controllers into services)
flagship_own.tests: No real coverage — only default Laravel stubs; README lists 'add automated tests' as a TODO.
flagship_own.relevance: high — strongest PHP piece: deliberate SOLID-style architecture + meaningful refactoring history + two non-trivial features.
flagship_own.caveat: Personal playground with unfinished TODOs and no actual tests despite phpunit setup — be honest if asked.

flagship_own.name: WordPress + React/TypeScript Article Plugin
flagship_own.description: A WordPress plugin ('article-app') embedding a React/TypeScript SPA into WordPress via a shortcode and a custom Gutenberg editor button; the SPA fetches articles/users/categories through the WP REST API and renders an article grid.
learnings: Bridging a modern React/TS SPA into a legacy PHP CMS
Dynamic asset registration for hashed Vite build filenames
Generic, typed API-call base component (typed contracts)
Reproducible local dev via DDEV pre-stop/post-start DB hooks
flagship_own.relevance: high — real iterative full-stack PHP + React/TS work with clear engineering reasoning.
flagship_own.caveat: README reads like a candidate submission (login creds, 'what I'd do with more time') — almost certainly a job take-home. No tests; committed WP core/node_modules hurt repo hygiene.
